THEFT OF SCRAP IRON FROM BOATS ON
THE SOOCHOW CREEK.
------------------------------------

At 8.45 a.m. 11-12-38 Mr. Z. Horikoshi, manager of
the Tokushima Gumi Co., 24 The Bund, came to the Station
and made the following complaint:-

He is engaged in the purchase of scrap iron for
export. About 3 weeks ago he entered into a contract
with the Toyoda Cotton Mill, 200 Jessfield Road, for the
purchase of 2,000 tons of broken up machinery. Delivery
commenced at once, and he engaged about 50 boats to
transport the cargo along the Soochow Creek from the mill
premises to the Whangpoo River.

The boats, supplied by a Chinese named "Tsai"(秦)
were furnished with permits allowing free entry through
occupied areas, and each boat was loaded with about 35
tons of the scrap iron. Two or three boatloads were
carried each day.

Mr. Horikoshi has discovered that when the boats
arrived at the river, their cargoes were considerably
depleted. Such depletion could only occur in transit
from the mill, and Mr. Horikoshi sent his employees to
try and find out how and where the scrap iron was
disposed.

quantities of the scrap iron had been delivered to an

杂项案号 521/38。静安寺路
1938年12月11日。
1.

苏州河船只废铁失窃案。
---

1938年12月11日上午8时45分，外滩24号德岛组（Tokushima Gumi Co.）经理堀越 Z. 先生（Mr. Z. Horikoshi）来到警局，提出如下投诉：

他从事废铁收购出口业务。约三周前，他与位于极司菲尔路200号的丰田棉纺厂（Toyoda Cotton Mill）签订合同，购买2,000吨拆解后的机器设备。交货随即开始，他雇用了约50艘船只，沿苏州河将货物从工厂码头运至黄浦江。

这些船只由一名姓“秦”（Tsai）的中国人提供，并配有允许自由通过占领区的通行证，每艘船装载约35吨废铁。每天运送两到三船。

堀越先生发现，当船只抵达江边时，货物数量大幅减少。这种短缺只可能发生在从工厂运输的途中，因此堀越先生派遣其雇员去调查废铁是如何以及在何处被处置的。
